result:
Both bugs fixed, tests added, shared code extracted — `bash tests/run_tests.sh` passes all 11 checks.

- `rotate.sh`: the guard used `-lt`, so exactly-N archives fell through to rotation; and `surplus()` did `tail -n +N` on a list sorted oldest-first, which kept the oldest and deleted from the N-th line onward (the newest). Now `-le` and `head -n "$((total - keep))"`, deleting only the oldest surplus. `head -n 0` is unreachable because the guard returns when `total <= keep`.
- `verify.sh`: `awk '{print $2}'` cut the archive name at its first space, so `my backup-….tar.gz` looked missing and was reported BAD. The digest is now the leading field and the name is the rest of the line (two-space separator); malformed means "no separator at all". Also quoted the digest comparison.
- `lib/common.sh` (new): `is_uint`, `need_value`, `resolve_dir` and the parser as `parse_options`, with a double-source guard. `rotate.sh` and `verify.sh` source it and call `parse_options "$@"`; `usage`/`parse_local_option` stay in each script and are looked up at call time. I re-checked the flags and exit codes against the old behaviour: `--help`, `--dest`/`--dest=`, `--name`, `--keep`, `-q`, `-n`, `--`, unknown option (1), missing value (1), `--keep 7x` (1), `--keep 0` (1), positional rejection (1), missing dest (2). `backup.sh`, `restore.sh` and `report.sh` are untouched, so they keep their own copy — note that `docs/DESIGN.md` §6 and wish-list item 1 now describe that split only as a plan, and I left the docs as they are.

Changed files: `rotate.sh`, `verify.sh`, `tests/run_tests.sh`, and new `lib/common.sh`.
